news_drafts.headline: Bridgend plans £8.5m borrowing for 2026-27 capital programme and covers £99.5m of need from its own cash
news_drafts.lead:
Bridgend County Borough Council's Cabinet is being given a revised capital programme (money spent on things that last, such as buildings, roads and vehicles) of £86.752m for 2026-27. Of that, £8.489m is to be paid for by borrowing, about 9.8% of the programme. The Cabinet meets on 20 October 2026.

The borrowing splits into £4.640m of unsupported borrowing, which the government does not support, and £3.849m of supported borrowing. The capital report for the second quarter of 2026-27 lists both as the council's own resources for the programme.

A separate appendix covers the council's capital financing requirement (the total it has spent on long-lived assets that it has not yet paid for, in effect its underlying need to borrow). It puts the estimate for 2026-27 at £207.026m, against estimated gross debt of £107.516m. The £99.510m gap is met from the council's own cash. The appendix says: "The capital borrowing need (Capital Financing Requirement) has not been fully funded with loan debt as cash supporting the Council's reserves, balances and cash flow has been used as a temporary measure. This is known as Internal Borrowing."

news_drafts.headline: Bridgend's 2025-26 accounts receive unqualified audit opinion
news_drafts.lead: The Auditor General for Wales intends to issue an unqualified audit opinion on Bridgend's 2025-26 accounts, confirming they give a true and fair view and were properly prepared. However, auditors identified several control weaknesses. The initial draft accounts did not include transactions and balances from the South East Wales Corporate Joint Committee, a shared body run with other councils, which were added only in a revised draft submitted in September. Auditors found that a category of asset valuations had not been properly indexed, a control gap that could become cumulatively significant over the five-year valuation cycle, though the current-year impact is not significant. Additionally, the minimum revenue provision—the amount set aside annually from the budget to repay borrowing—was understated by £0.291 million due to the accounting treatment of the Rhiw property purchase. All issues were corrected during the audit.

news_drafts.headline: Bridgend's 2025-26 accounts certified early, but audit found multiple errors in draft figures
news_drafts.lead: Bridgend Council's external auditors are certifying the 2025-26 accounts on 25 September, six days ahead of the statutory 30 September deadline. The Governance and Audit Committee was told that auditors had identified a series of misstatements in the draft accounts, all later corrected by council officers. These included member allowances overstated by £0.061 million, minimum revenue provision (the amount the council must set aside from each year's budget to repay past borrowing) understated by £0.291 million, transactions from the South East Wales Corporate Joint Committee initially omitted, and property valuations that had not been updated. The auditor also flagged that indexation, the annual revaluation uplift applied to council property assets, has not been applied to a category of existing use value assets and could become cumulatively material over five years. The council's previous year accounts received a clean bill of health from auditors.

findings.paper_title: 4a - Appendix 1 - Prior Year Budget Reductions Monitoring
findings.headline: A £60k saving from relocating the Tythegston recycling centre to Pyle, ending lease payments at the old site, is expected in full in 2026-27.
findings.detail: The new site opened in quarter 4 of 2023-24. The saving was not achieved in 2025-26 because the lease exit terms were still being worked through, and the paper says it will be made in full in 2026-27.
findings.matters: A saving that was delayed by lease exit terms has now been resolved and is expected in full, which is a useful reference for other councils with similar lease-exit timing.
findings.quote: The new site opened during quarter 4 of 2023-24

findings.paper_title: 4a - Appendix 1 - Prior Year Budget Reductions Monitoring
findings.headline: A £142k saving in the CART ancillary support area is expected to contribute nothing in 2026-27, with a review aiming to delegate funding to schools from April 2027.
findings.detail: The paper says a review of CART ancillary support is under way and that delegating some funding to schools is expected to reduce the high level of overspend in that area. Until then, the directorate must identify alternative savings if the shortfall is not reduced.
findings.matters: A service carrying a high overspend while its planned saving is deferred to a future year is the pattern a finance director needs to watch, and the paper names the delegation date.
findings.figures: 142 original reduction; 0 expected in 2026-27; delegation anticipated from April 2027
findings.quote: reduce the high level of overspend in this area

findings.paper_title: 4a - Appendix 1 - Prior Year Budget Reductions Monitoring
findings.headline: The commercial letting of Pandy Depot is expected to deliver £13k of a £50k saving in 2026-27, with the balance expected in 2027-28.
findings.detail: The paper says ongoing efforts to let the depot did not reach agreement by the end of 2025-26, and that vacancy savings in Corporate Landlord covered the shortfall. Operational requirements have delayed the letting decision.
findings.matters: Property income savings that depend on a letting decision can move a year or more, and a council planning around them needs to know the timing as well as the amount.
findings.figures: 50 original reduction; 13 expected in 2026-27; full achievement expected in 2027-28
findings.quote: In view of operational requirements resulting in delaying the letting decision this

findings.paper_title: 4a - Appendix 1 - Prior Year Budget Reductions Monitoring
findings.headline: A £35k saving from letting the former Woodmat property has moved to 2027-28, with £0 expected in 2026-27 because the lease contract is still being finalised.
findings.detail: The paper says the savings have been made elsewhere within the service in the short term, through staff vacancies. It says the saving is now anticipated to be fully achieved in 2027-28.
findings.matters: A property letting that slips a full year leaves a budget gap that is covered only by vacancies, which are temporary.
findings.figures: 35 original reduction; 0 expected in 2026-27; fully achieved anticipated in 2027-28
findings.quote: Delays due to the finalisation of the contract for the lease

findings.paper_title: 4a - Appendix 1 - Prior Year Budget Reductions Monitoring
findings.headline: Pest control charging, which was not achieved, led BCBC to stop providing the service from 31 October 2025, and alternative budgets have been identified for its £3,950 net cost.
findings.detail: The paper says reduced uptake of the domestic pest control service led to the decision to stop providing it. The £67k saving was not achieved in full in 2025-26, and the service's underlying net budget of £3,950 is being covered by alternative budgets.
findings.matters: Ending a service rather than making it pay for itself is a route other councils may take when a charging saving fails, and it leaves a residual budget to be offset.
findings.figures: 67 original reduction; 67 expected in 2026-27; net budget £3,950
findings.quote: Alternative budgets to mitigate the underlying net budget of £3,950 for the service
